_comment: Per-image load geometry for tools/decomp_pipeline.py. DATA, not code: adding a title or an
overlay is an entry here, and the pipeline checks what it can about each one before it imports
KIND decides what is checked, and it is a field rather than a branch in the code:
'resident' -- a PS-X EXE. Load address, text size and entry come from its OWN header, and the
numbers here are CROSS-CHECKED against it; a disagreement is a refusal, because a wrong base
imports cleanly and puts every function at a plausible address that is not the recorded one.
'module'   -- an overlay (.PRG / .BIN). NO header, NO entry, and no address derivable from
the file, so load_base and the code window are the OWNING PORT'S MEASURED facts and are
trusted as data. What the tool can still check is that the code window lies inside the FILE,
that the base is in 2 MiB of KSEG0, and the sha1 gate below.
ghidra_base is DERIVED, never stored, so it cannot drift:
resident -> text_load_address - text_file_offset (which maps file offset 0x800 onto the load
address and leaves the executable's own header below the text window),
module   -> load_base (a module's text begins at file offset 0).
MEASURED 2026-09-28/29 from the provisioned images. Every resident title in this workspace is a
PS-X EXE loading at 0x80010000 with text at file offset 0x800; they differ in text size, which is
why the size is data here rather than an assumption in the code.

spyro1.note: Insomniac. Its repo verified the file-offset formula against 62,183 of 62,183 recorded instructions.

crash1.note: Naughty Dog. Retail projection is H=1000, OFX=0, OFY=0; widening must not raise the 0x800578D0 GTE near plane.

crashbash.note: Main image has no file extension; find -iname 'SCUS*.BIN' misses it. Has 7 overlays, not yet declared.

ctr.note: Naughty Dog. Measured 2 fields per game frame; 30 fps.

megamanx4.note: Capcom. Its text is 2.83x spyro1's and MEASURED to fit the 1400 MB ceiling: 4,834 functions, up to 1,089,096 KB peak RSS, 53.3 s. NOTE 0x80015FE0 is NOT a function entry (nearest entry 0x80016004, +0x24) and 0x80015FD4 is +264 INSIDE FUN_80015ecc's body; both are labels, not entries.

spiderman1.note: Neversoft. Reaches library routines through jalr function pointers, so a jal-only census reads 0 for every one of them.

tekken3.note: Namco. Already 60 fps, so widescreen-only enhancement scope.

tomba1.note: Whoopee Camp. Already 60 fps, so widescreen-only enhancement scope.

tomba2.note: Whoopee Camp. The resident executable is ~15% of the title; most code is in .PRG overlays loaded at run time. Has overlays, not yet declared.

vagrant.note: Square. SHA-1 of this image MATCHES the CC0 rood-reverse decomp's declared target, so its symbol addresses are confirmed against real bytes -- a reading aid only, never copied into a shipping path. 933,925 B of its code lives in .PRG overlays; see the vagrant_* modules.

vagrant_battle.title: vagrant
vagrant_battle.note: BATTLE.PRG, 577,828 B on disc (BATTLE.BIN). code_first/code_last are the MEASURED CODE EXTENT (the decomp declares 0x146C..0x7F984), and code_first is NOT 0: the module's first words are a POINTER TABLE (0x8006C684 = base+0x3E84, and eight consecutive words all resolve inside the module), so disassembly seeded at file offset 0 reaches nothing. Verified here: offset 0x146C holds 0x27BDFFE8, an `addiu $sp,$sp,-N` prologue, which is what a code extent starts with. Load base is the vagrant repo's MEASURED fact (tools/re_viewport.py BATTLE_LOAD_BASE, itself derived in tools/re_overlay.py M2 from this module's own absolute jal targets and entry offsets -- 20/20 identity and address agreements, and the decomp declares the same vram). Its decomp-declared CODE extent is 0x146C..0x7F984; that is narrower than the loaded module and is where its functions live, but the pipeline seeds disassembly at the window start and reports what it finds. HOLDS func_800760CC, the port's projection owner.

vagrant_title.title: vagrant
vagrant_title.note: TITLE.PRG, 554,568 B (TITLE.BIN). Same measured load base as BATTLE -- they SHARE one slot, which is exactly why a guest address is meaningless without the module identity, and why a resident-only reader could never decompile both. Declared code extent 0x22C..0x959C.

vagrant_initbtl.title: vagrant
vagrant_initbtl.note: INITBTL.PRG, 7,036 B (INITBTL.BIN). A DIFFERENT measured base from BATTLE/TITLE -- 0x800F9800 against 0x80068800 -- which is what makes it the control: the same reader, the same code path, a base 0x91000 away. Its decomp-declared code extent is 0x18..0x1318.
